strings.settings.name: Name
strings.landing.title: Know what changed about your access, before you're refused
strings.landing.lede: A companion for journalists covering the 2026 World Cup. It shows what your accreditation currently permits, what has changed about it, and the reason attached to each change — so you find out from this screen rather than by being turned away at a barrier.
strings.landing.disclosureStrong: This is a portfolio demonstration, not a FIFA product.
strings.landing.disclosureBody: It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to FIFA. Every record, holder and decision in it is simulated. The match schedule is real; nothing else is.
strings.landing.signedOutBody: The simulated session has ended. Signing in again, as either holder, starts a new one.
strings.signIn.title: Sign in
strings.signIn.noticeBody: There is no account system behind it — the credentials below are fake, but they work. Refreshing the page signs you out, since the session lives only in this tab. It is not a security boundary and it protects nothing.
strings.signIn.accountsIntro: These are published, fake demo credentials — not real accounts, and nothing to keep secret. Sign in with either:
strings.signIn.failure: That identifier and password do not match a demo account. Both are published above.
strings.signIn.identifierLength: This must be between 3 and 120 characters.
strings.signIn.identifierAllowed: Use letters, numbers, spaces, and the marks . - ' _ @ only.
strings.record.title: My Requests
strings.record.signedOut: This record belongs to a holder, so it asks who you are first.
strings.record.signedOutLink: Sign in with one of the two published demo accounts
strings.record.signedOutAfter: — neither of them protects anything, and the sign-in page says so.
strings.record.errorHeading: No access state is available offline
strings.record.errorBody1: Your record could not be loaded and nothing is stored on this device yet, so this app cannot tell you what you currently hold.
strings.record.errorBody2: Do not rely on this screen at a barrier. Take your credential to the accreditation desk and ask them to read your current state from their own system.
strings.record.emptyBody: Nothing has been issued against this credential number. If you have applied, your application is still with the accreditation team and has not reached a decision — that stage has no updates to show, and this screen will fill in once it does.
strings.record.emptyLink: What this service does and does not cover

strings.record.withdrawConfirmPrompt: Withdraw your request for this match? It stays visible in your record either way.
strings.record.refreshFailed: The last attempt to refresh this failed. What you see above is the state stored on this device, at the time shown.
strings.record.noChangesAfter: Silence here means nothing has moved, not that nothing has been checked.

strings.help.title: Help
strings.help.intro: This app shows what your accreditation currently permits, what has changed about it, and why. It is not the accreditation system itself, and it cannot change any decision that system has taken.
strings.help.hint: Every section is closed to begin with. Open the one you came for.
strings.help.beforeApply.heading: Before you apply
strings.help.beforeApply.body: Nothing appears here until an application exists against your credential number. Applications are made through your member association, your broadcaster, or the freelance route — not through this app.
strings.help.beingAssessed.heading: While your application is being assessed
strings.help.beingAssessed.body: This is the longest silence in the whole process, and this app cannot shorten it. There are no interim stages to report during assessment, so an empty record here means your application has not yet reached a decision — not that it has been overlooked.
strings.help.decision.heading: Once a decision is taken
strings.help.decision.body: The decision appears as a change, with the reason attached and whatever you can do next. Approval is always stated as approved until a date, because it is never open-ended.
strings.help.tournament.heading: During the tournament
strings.help.tournament.body: Your access can move after approval — quotas contract, zone lists get revised, and some entitlements depend on results that have not happened yet. Every one of those movements is written here before it takes effect, so you find out by reading rather than by being turned away.
strings.help.matchday.heading: On a matchday
strings.help.matchday.body: The state on this screen is the last one your device managed to fetch, and it always shows its own age. Check that age before you rely on it. If the venue's list disagrees with what you see, this app records the disagreement and points you at a person — it does not settle it.
strings.help.notDo.heading: What this service does not do
strings.help.notDo.visasBody: Nothing here affects your right to enter any host country, and this app does not know your visa status.
strings.help.notDo.vettingBody: Security vetting is carried out elsewhere and its reasoning is not shared with this app.
strings.help.notDo.quotaBody: How many places your association or broadcaster receives, and who gets them, is decided outside this app entirely.
strings.help.notDo.guaranteeBody: Nothing shown here is a promise. An entitlement recorded today can be changed tomorrow, which is exactly why the record exists.
strings.help.notDo.appealsBody: There is no appeal channel in this app, and the contact section is not one.
strings.help.notNotify.heading: What will not reach you as a notification
strings.help.notNotify.intro: Some changes are written to your record without interrupting you. They are still there to read; they simply do not raise an alert. If they did, the alerts that matter would be buried among them.
strings.help.notNotify.item1: Corrections to administrative details that do not affect what you can do.
strings.help.notNotify.item3: Access being widened — a zone or a match added rather than removed.
strings.help.notNotify.item4: Your existing state being re-confirmed without changing.
strings.help.notNotify.closing: This list is published for one reason: an unexplained silence is indistinguishable from a broken app. If nothing has reached you, you should be able to check here and know why.
strings.help.contact.heading: Who to contact
strings.help.contact.intro: This app does not accept submissions, and sending something here would not reach anyone. Contact the people who already hold your file:
strings.help.contact.officerStrong: Your member association or broadcaster media officer
strings.help.contact.officerBody: — for anything about quota, allocation, or which of your colleagues holds which place.
strings.help.contact.centreStrong: The accreditation centre in the host city
strings.help.contact.centreBody: — for a credential that will not scan, a lost pass, or a disagreement at a barrier.
strings.help.contact.fifaBody: — for a decision you believe was recorded against the wrong person or the wrong match.
strings.help.contact.mocked: Contact routes are described here in general terms. This version of the app is a demonstration and carries no live contact details or integrations.
